summary: Brushed off by the body: You speak about {the problem} during public comment and {district member} brushes you off in front of {presiding officer}.
realLife: One life: In 1988, as a private citizen, he told the Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, council about storm runoff piped into a wetland and felt brushed off. He ran for mayor in 1990 and beat an 18-year incumbent. Another: He emailed Somerville, Massachusetts, council members after each crash at the corner by his apartment until the city added a turn arrow in 2025, then ran for the council that year.
gates: {the problem} is on record and {the body} has the power to act on it.
A meeting with public comment is on the calendar.
weights: How much {the problem} has cost your household.
choices: press with what happened and who was hurt
ask who can act on it and when
say you will come back with neighbors
after a dismissive answer only: say the seat needs someone who listens

branches.then: A member moves to fix it and it passes. You are known as the one who got it done, a fact the filing scenes read.
{presiding officer} knows your name before you reach the microphone, and {district member} becomes the incumbent you would face.

branches.when: your job is covering {the body} for {outlet}
branches.then: You know the file better than the members, and speaking up puts your job's neutrality at stake.
That night {household member} asks whether you mean to do something about it.
